message.content:
Based on my search, here is a comprehensive overview of **calcium-containing foods**:

## Dairy Products (Highest Natural Sources)

Dairy products are among the most concentrated and well-absorbed sources of calcium:

| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|-----------------|
| Dried skimmed milk powder (100g) | ~1,590 mg |
| Yogurt, plain low-fat (8 oz/1 cup) | 415-448 mg |
| Milk, nonfat/skim (1 cup) | 299-325 mg |
| Milk, whole (1 cup) | 276-300 mg |
| Mozzarella, part-skim (1.5 oz) | 333 mg |
| Cheddar cheese (1.5 oz) | 306 mg |
| Ricotta, part-skim (1/2 cup) | 337 mg |
| Cottage cheese, 1% fat (1 cup) | 138-276 mg |

## Non-Dairy Animal Sources

| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|-----------------|
| Sardines, canned with bones (3 oz) | 324-325 mg |
| Salmon, pink canned with bones (3 oz) | 181 mg |
| Pilchards/Sardines in tomato sauce (100g) | 250-430 mg |

## Plant-Based Sources

### Vegetables & Leafy Greens
| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|-----------------|
| Collard greens, cooked (1 cup) | 324 mg |
| Kale, cooked (1 cup) | 177 mg |
| Okra, stir-fried (100g) | 220 mg |
| Bok choy/Chinese cabbage (1 cup) | 74-158 mg |
| Broccoli, cooked (1 cup) | 62-76 mg |
| Turnip greens, boiled (1/2 cup) | 99 mg |

**Note:** Spinach contains high oxalic acid, which reduces calcium absorption to only about 5%, compared to 27-30% from milk and low-oxalate greens like kale and bok choy.

### Legumes, Soy Products & Nuts
| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|-----------------|
| Tofu, firm with calcium sulfate (1/2 cup) | 253-553 mg |
| Tofu, soft with calcium sulfate (1/2 cup) | 138 mg |
| Edamame, cooked (1 cup) | 130 mg |
| Sesame seeds (100g) | 670 mg |
| Chia seeds (1 tablespoon) | 76-179 mg |
| Almonds (1 oz) | 76 mg |

### Fortified Foods
| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|-----------------|
| Calcium-fortified orange juice (1 cup) | 349 mg |
| Soy milk, fortified (1 cup) | 299-399 mg |
| Almond milk, fortified (1 cup) | 482 mg |
| Breakfast cereals, fortified (1 serving) | 100-1,000 mg |
| Rice milk, fortified (1 cup) | 300 mg |

### Other Sources
| Food | Calcium Content |
|------|-----------------|
| Dried figs (4) | 54-250 mg |
| Oranges (1 medium) | 60-65 mg |
| Blackberries (1 cup) | 42 mg |

## Key Points

- **Absorption matters:** Calcium from dairy and fortified foods is absorbed at about 30%. Some plant foods like spinach have much lower absorption (5%) due to oxalic acid, while low-oxalate greens like kale, broccoli, and bok choy have absorption rates similar to milk.
- **Fortified foods** can provide significant calcium for those who don't consume dairy.
- **Vitamin D** is essential for proper calcium absorption.

Sources:
1. https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Calcium-HealthProfessional/
2. https://www.health.harvard.edu/nutrition/calcium-rich-foods-how-to-boost-your-intake-of-this-important-mineral
3. https://www.health.harvard.edu/diet-and-nutrition/calcium-rich-foods-how-to-boost-your-intake-of-this-important-mineral
4. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK45523/table/ch7.t2/
5. https://www.webmd.com/diet/foods-high-in-calcium
6. https://gp-training.hee.nhs.uk/windsor/wp-content/uploads/sites/96/2021/09/Vitamin-D-testing-and-treatment-guidelines.pdf
7. https://imsear.searo.who.int/bitstreams/99ce16a3-83a5-4fba-8f33-d0c9a0428303/download
8. https://www.bucksformulary.nhs.uk/docs/Guideline_307FM.pdf
9. https://www.bucksformulary.nhs.uk/docs/Guideline_834FM.pdf?uid=598797444&uid2=2020111220184122
